newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Timetable for Dublin European Union summit.
newsitem.headline: Timetable for Dublin European Union summit.

text.p: Following is the official agenda for the two-day European summit starting in Dublin on Friday at Dublin Castle.
The summit will be attended by heads of state and government from the EU's 15 members. They will also meet their counterparts from central and eastern Europe, the Baltic states and Cyprus.

The formal agenda will focus on progress of economic and monetary union (EMU), the EU's inter-governmental conference (IGC) and the fight against unemployment, drugs and organised crime. External relations issues will be discussed during working lunches and dinners.
FRIDAY, DECEMBER 13
* 1000 GMT Meeting between European Parliament President Klaus Haensch and EU leaders.
* 1030 GMT First working session, in presence of EU economic and finance ministers. Agenda includes:
- Decision on reappointment of European Monetary Institute (EMI) President Alexandre Lamfalussy from January 1, 1997, and appointment of Wim Duisenberg as EMI president from July 1, 1997.

- Discussions on the legal framework for the euro single currency, the EMU budget stability pact and a new exchange rate mechanism - the ERM2 - which will link the euro with EU currencies staying outside.
- Discussion on ways to reinforce the strategy to create employment.
* 1300 GMT Irish President Mary Robinson hosts lunch in honour of leaders and European Parliament President Klaus Haensch.
* 1500 GMT Second working session. Agenda includes:
- Adoption of declarations on organised crime and the fight against drugs.
- Discussion on status of the inter-governmental conference (IGC) and the Irish presidency's draft EU treaty.
- European Commission President Jacques Santer gives oral report on preparations for EU enlargement.
* 1900 GMT Irish presidency holds news conference on the outcome of the first and second working sessions.
* 2000 GMT Separate working dinners of EU leaders and foreign ministers at the National Gallery of Ireland.

- EU leaders are expected to discuss relations with eastern countries, especially Russia, Ukraine and Belarus; the Council of Europe's role in promoting human rights and the rule of law; EU-U.S. relations in view of forthcoming bilateral summit; Great Lakes region of Africa and Zaire.
- EU foreign ministers are expected to discuss the situation in the former Yugoslavia, the Middle East, the Great Lakes region and Zaire, and Turkey.
SATURDAY, DECEMBER 14
* 1000 GMT Third working session devoted to finalising the summit conclusions.
* 1300 GMT Separate working lunches of EU leaders and foreign ministers and their counterparts from central and eastern Europe, the Baltic states and Cyprus:
- Leaders are expected to discuss common challenge of combatting international crime, particularly trafficking in drugs and people.
- Foreign ministers are expected to discuss the situation in Russia, Belarus and the former Yugoslavia.
* 1500 GMT Fourth working session with those participants to discuss future relations and the outcome of the summit.

* 1630 GMT (Possibly) Fifth working session - followed by a joint news conference by Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring and European Commission President Jacques Santer.
* 2000 GMT EU foreign ministers and Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller attend working dinner.
